_what: Where Messages reads the person's conversations (chat-records.ts). This file names only roles and the SQL, with {table} and {titles} where the table goes: each role's connection and table come from the owner-places record in the person's own records (workspace_records, label owner-places, value {"roles": {role: {credential_name, table}}}). A store whose role has no record is not read. `list` answers the newest conversations, at most $1, as rows of source, chat, last, name, words (the newest line, cut short), mine and sender. `page` answers one conversation's lines newest first: $1 the source, $2 the chat, $3 a time to read before (or null), $4 the most lines; rows of id, at, words, mine, author and media (JSON of the photos and files of the line). `forget` (the told store) takes one line out of the person's history by its id ($1), setting erased_at. Every statement is sent with statement_timeout_ms: a statement that runs longer is stopped. Replying is off in `reply` until its tool is offered by a computer. no_reply words are in messages-words.json.

stores.list: with chats as (select source, after->>'chat' as chat, max(at) as last from {table} where place = 'message' and erased_at is null and after->>'chat' is not null group by 1, 2 order by 3 desc limit $1), newest as (select distinct on (source, after->>'chat') source, after->>'chat' as chat, after from {table} where place = 'message' and erased_at is null and (source, after->>'chat') in (select source, chat from chats) order by source, after->>'chat', at desc) select c.source, c.chat, c.last::text as last, (select s.after->>'chat_name' from {table} s where s.place = 'message' and s.source = c.source and s.after->>'chat' = c.chat and s.after->>'chat_name' is not null limit 1) as name, left(coalesce(n.after->>'words', ''), 200) as words, coalesce(n.after->>'from', 'x') = '' as mine, n.after->>'from' as sender from chats c join newest n using (source, chat) order by c.last desc
stores.page: select id::text as id, at::text as at, left(coalesce(after->>'words', ''), 1500) as words, coalesce(after->>'from', 'x') = '' as mine, nullif(after->>'from', '') as author, coalesce(after->'media', '[]'::jsonb)::text as media from {table} where place = 'message' and source = $1 and after->>'chat' = $2 and erased_at is null and ($3::timestamptz is null or at < $3::timestamptz) order by at desc, id desc limit $4
stores.forget: update {table} set erased_at = now() where place = 'message' and erased_at is null and id = $1::bigint returning id::text as id

stores.list: with chats as (select app as source, conversation_id as chat, max(at) as last from {table} group by 1, 2 order by 3 desc limit $1), newest as (select distinct on (conversation_id) conversation_id as chat, text, speaker from {table} where conversation_id in (select chat from chats) order by conversation_id, at desc) select c.source, c.chat, c.last, (select a.title from {titles} a where a.conversation_id = c.chat limit 1) as name, left(coalesce(n.text, ''), 200) as words, n.speaker = 'person' as mine, n.speaker as sender from chats c left join newest n using (chat) order by c.last desc
stores.page: select coalesce(source_ref, conversation_id || ':' || at) as id, at, left(coalesce(text, ''), 1500) as words, speaker = 'person' as mine, case when speaker in ('ai', 'person') then null else speaker end as author, '[]' as media from {table} where app = $1 and conversation_id = $2 and ($3::text is null or at < $3::text) order by at desc limit $4

contacts.list: select regexp_replace(phone, '\D', '', 'g') as digits, name from {table} where name is not null and name <> '' and phone ~ '\d' and source like '%Mac Contacts%' limit $1

reply._what: The tool that sends a reply for a told conversation whose store names reply_source: one message to one recipient, the handle of a one-to-one chat (its chat id ends in the handle). The Mac's Messages app sends it; the answer says per recipient what was sent or what failed. `enabled` is off until a computer that offers the capability `use-the-messages-app` is asked by that tool: today tool:send-a-message-on-this-mac is refused with 'No computer asked offers it' (checked Nov 21), so the composer stays disabled.
